submissions.findingTextShort: A 12-person crossover study detected aspalathin/nothofagin metabolites after rooibos tea or an active rooibos fraction, with no significant increase in plasma antioxidant capacity by ORAC.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: In a complete crossover study, 12 healthy men consumed placebo, rooibos tea, or an active rooibos fraction. Multiple metabolites of aspalathin and nothofagin were detected, while unchanged plasma flavonoids were only trace-level and plasma antioxidant capacity measured by ORAC did not significantly increase. This is direct human exposure/pharmacokinetic and biomarker-null evidence for rooibos-derived aspalathin exposure, not isolated-aspalathin metabolic or antioxidant clinical efficacy.
submissions.populationContext: Twelve healthy men in a complete crossover exposure study.
submissions.usageContext: Rooibos tea and an active rooibos fraction; multicomponent food-matrix exposure rather than isolated aspalathin supplementation.
submissions.mechanismContext: Human absorption/metabolism of rooibos flavonoids with no significant ORAC plasma-antioxidant-capacity increase.
submissions.uncertaintyNote: Very small sample and multicomponent interventions. Metabolite detection confirms exposure, not therapeutic benefit or an isolated-compound dose response.

submissions.findingTextShort: A 10-volunteer rooibos study found urinary aspalathin metabolites but low overall recovery, supporting limited food-matrix bioavailability rather than efficacy.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: Ten volunteers consumed fermented and unfermented rooibos teas in a human bioavailability study. Urinary metabolites of aspalathin were detected, but overall recovery was low. Fermentation state, the tea matrix, co-flavonoids and metabolite identity are part of the exposure proposition. These findings establish absorption/metabolism context and must not be converted into isolated-aspalathin treatment efficacy or a generic supplement dosing claim.
submissions.populationContext: Ten human volunteers in a rooibos-tea bioavailability study.
submissions.usageContext: Fermented and unfermented rooibos tea; food-matrix exposure.
submissions.uncertaintyNote: Small PK study with low recovery. No clinical efficacy endpoint was established.

submissions.findingTextShort: Six-subject human work showed intact aspalathin can be absorbed and undergo methylation/glucuronidation, a PK finding rather than clinical efficacy.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: Human work in six participants demonstrated that intact aspalathin can be absorbed after rooibos exposure and undergo methylation and glucuronidation. This supports direct human pharmacokinetic plausibility but does not establish a clinical metabolic, antioxidant, cardiovascular or neurobehavioral benefit for isolated aspalathin.
submissions.populationContext: Six human participants in an absorption/metabolism study.
submissions.usageContext: Rooibos-derived exposure; not a defined isolated-aspalathin therapeutic regimen.
submissions.uncertaintyNote: Tiny sample and PK-only endpoints prevent efficacy inference.

submissions.findingTextShort: Available human evidence is predominantly rooibos food-matrix PK/metabolite research and does not establish isolated-aspalathin clinical efficacy or safety.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: The directly resolved human evidence in this research pass predominantly measures exposure, absorption and metabolites after rooibos tea or rooibos fractions rather than administering isolated aspalathin as a clinical intervention. Therefore rooibos outcomes, PK signals or ordinary beverage safety cannot be inherited as isolated-aspalathin efficacy, consumer dosing or comprehensive safety. The isolated-compound profile should remain evidence-limited/NOINDEX until direct intervention evidence is governed.
submissions.usageContext: Evidence-identity firewall between rooibos food/extract matrices and isolated aspalathin.
submissions.uncertaintyNote: This is a proposition-level research gap, not proof that no future isolated-human trial exists. Revalidate when new direct evidence is found.
